obligations.note: The change adds `coapplicant_tax_id`, a tax identifier and so NPI, to ApplicantFields.ALL but not to NpiRegistry.FIELDS or the approved `mortgage.npi_fields` list. The field is therefore persisted unsealed through the existing pipeline. The ENC-1 control test only enumerates the registry, so a pass cannot catch this omission.

Retention.purge now also removes `coapplicant_tax_id`, and the due/hold logic in isPurgeDue is unchanged. The only test evidence is the sample-coverage RetentionControlTest, and the reports that contain it cannot be tied to this change's CI run (see CHG-4).

Ticket CHG-25472 is standard and was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-01, before review. Its components (mortgage.cases, mortgage.retention, mortgage.control-tests) cover all three touched paths.
Declan Farrell, a change_approver for baseline-mortgage and not the author (Tomas Ortega), approved code_review on the head commit 0593a1c.
The change has one commit. The code_review and control_owner approvals both name the head commit 0593a1c.

run.json says ci-runner-08 ran on 0593a1c at 2026-10-02. The attached JUnit reports were produced on host dev-laptop-7.local, timestamped 2026-10-23, which is after the review time of 2026-10-07. The reports do not belong to this CI run, so no valid evidence shows the full suite and control tests passing on the final commit.
The touched components (mortgage.cases, mortgage.retention, mortgage.control-tests) are none of them marked security_sensitive, so no security_review approval is required.

ControlFixtures.java sits under the protected path apps/baseline-mortgage/src/test/java/controls/*. Rachel Stein (control_owner, controls-office team, outside the author's lending-eng team) approved the head commit.
The change is not an emergency (emergency=false, ticket type standard), so no PIR is due.
No exception in the register covers ENC-1 for mortgage.cases or mortgage.store. The unsealed NPI field is therefore an unexcepted deviation from a product obligation.
The ledger entries cover Approvals.java, Policy.java, Underwriting.java and payments files, none of which this change touches. No accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The change introduces a co-applicant tax identifier, which is NPI under ENC-1. It is added to the applicant field list without being registered in NpiRegistry or the approved npi_fields, so it is stored unsealed. No exception covers this deviation. Separately, the attached JUnit reports come from a developer machine and are dated after the review time, so they do not evidence a CI run on the head commit. Ticketing and approvals are otherwise in order, but the ENC-1 violation and the invalid test evidence require rejection.
